official.deadline_note: One central LFU:online closing date for all faculties; no separate faculty deadlines are published. Performance-based call AY 2025/26 ran 31 Aug - 02 Oct 2026 (previous cycle: 01 Sep - 03 Oct 2025); thesis scholarship had two windows, 04 - 22 May 2026 and 14 Sep - 02 Oct 2026 (previous cycle: 05 - 23 May 2025 and 15 Sep - 03 Oct 2025).
official.status_note: The published AY 2025/26 application windows closed on 02 October 2026 (performance-based 31 Aug - 02 Oct 2026; theses 14 Sep - 02 Oct 2026). The College Service Center keeps the calls online and republishes them for each new academic year around late August / early May.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official information states that no grants are given for tuition fees; the performance-based scholarship is a one-time cash payment with no published tuition reduction.
benefits: Performance-based scholarships can amount to between EUR 750.00 and EUR 1500.00 and is a one-time payment.
Scholarships for scientific theses: at least EUR 750 / maximum EUR 3600 (one-off payment).
Scholarships for scientific theses can refund additional costs arising for students during periods spent away from where they live and study.
Literature can be financed only if the books are given to the university or faculty library once the thesis has been completed.
The university additionally signposts the Austrian student grant (Stipendienstelle Innsbruck / stipendium.at) with travel allowance, insurance cost subsidy, childcare subsidy and study allowance.
eligibility: Austrian citizens, citizens from EEA states and stateless persons granted equal status are entitled to make an application (StudFG section 3 and section 4).
Applicants must have a grade point average no lower than 2.0 for the examinations, courses and written pieces of work submitted.

Applicants must not exceed the maximum study period (regular duration of studies plus one semester); working and/or enrolment in a second study programme are no reasons for exceeding the maximum study time.
Applicants must have completed a minimum number of semester hours/ECTS-Credits in the year prior to the application; the number differs per faculty.
For scholarships for scientific theses: the diploma, master's or doctoral thesis must already be registered but not yet completed.
requirements: Only examinations registered in LFU:online with semester hours/ECTS-Credits and grades can be considered; courses graded 'successfully completed' cannot be counted.
The grade point average is calculated from individual grades; overall grades are not used.
For AY 2025/26 performance-based applications, examinations must date between 01 October 2025 and 30 September 2026; for recognitions the actual examination date counts.
Complete the application in full (telephone no., bank name, IBAN, BIC) in LFU:online before forwarding it to the College Service Center.

Faculty-specific thresholds, e.g. Architecture PhD at least 15 ECTS with GPA not greater than 1.0; Psychology and Sport Science Bachelor/Master at least 50 ECTS with GPA not greater than 1.20; Engineering Sciences Bachelor/Master at least 45 ECTS with GPA not greater than 1.50.
documents: Online application via the students' platform LFU:online (paper application form only in special cases, submitted in person).
For scholarships for scientific theses: description of the thesis.
For scholarships for scientific theses: overview of costs, completed in full and signed by the relevant expert.
For scholarships for scientific theses: financing plan (how the thesis has been and will be financed otherwise).
For scholarships for scientific theses: at least one expert opinion from a university teacher (section 94 paragraph 2 of the Universities Act 2002).
Optional: confirmation from the Austrian Students' Union of a student representative role for one additional semester of study extension.
Final report with invoices and receipts after thesis completion (recipients of thesis scholarships).
selection_criteria: The number of applications submitted always exceeds the number of scholarships available, so applications are ranked.
Ranking improves with more semester hours/ECTS-Credits submitted and a better grade point average.
Applicants do not have a legal right to receive a performance-based scholarship.

For theses: the expert opinion must demonstrate an eligible, exceptional financial burden, probable above-average grades and additional value for the university, including embedment in research or third-party funded projects.
coverage: One-off cash payment recognising exceptional academic performance (performance-based scholarship).
Thesis-related project costs for registered but not yet completed theses (scholarship for scientific theses).
Not covered: living costs, tuition fees, chemicals, long-term investment goods, binding of the thesis, and employment of staff (e.g. student workers).
Additional costs arising during periods spent away from the place of residence and study can be refunded if listed separately in the overview of costs.
application_method: Apply via the students' platform LFU:online within the published application period.
Students unable to apply via LFU:online can submit the application in person at the College Service Center, Innrain 52a, Ágnes Heller Haus, second floor, room 02M010, 6020 Innsbruck.
official.application_route: Submit online via LFU:online during the published window; paper filing in person at the College Service Center only if online application is not possible.
official.citizenship_residency: Austrian citizens, citizens from EEA states and stateless persons granted equal status (StudFG section 3 and section 4).
official.international_eligibility: Open to citizens of EU and other EEA states and to stateless persons granted equal status; third-country nationals are not entitled to apply under StudFG section 4.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicable to all degree programmes of the University of Innsbruck (Bachelor, Diploma, Master, Doctoral/PhD); for joint Innsbruck-Medical University and UMIT programmes the application can only be filed at the University of Innsbruck.
official.research_requirement: Scholarships for scientific theses are tied to a registered but not yet completed diploma, master's or doctoral thesis with supervisor expert opinion; the performance-based scholarship is purely grade and ECTS based.
official.duration: One-off payment, not a recurring stipend; performance-based scholarships are awarded for one academic year based on the previous year's examinations (01 October - 30 September).
official.description: Awarded under section 57 of the Austrian Federal Student Support Act (StudFG), performance-based scholarships recognise exceptional academic performance at the University of Innsbruck, while scholarships for scientific theses support students writing registered but not yet completed diploma, master's or doctoral theses. Both are administered centrally by the College Service Center, decided per faculty, and applied for through LFU:online in annual calls.
official.program_type: University-administered scholarships: performance-based scholarship (Leistungsstipendium) and scholarship for scientific theses (Foerderungsstipendium)

applicant_utility.summary: Despite the catalogue title, the University of Innsbruck does not run a scholarship reserved for international students: its two in-house schemes are legally limited to Austrian and EEA citizens under the StudFG. The performance-based scholarship pays EUR 750-1,500 once for top prior-year grades, and the thesis scholarship pays EUR 750-3,600 once for registered but unfinished theses. Both go through LFU:online in a single autumn window (late August to early October) plus an early-May window for theses, so non-EEA applicants should instead plan around the Austrian student grant (stipendium.at) or home-government funding. Already enrolled EU/EEA students can realistically aim here with a strong transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled (not prospective) EU/EEA students at Innsbruck with an excellent previous academic year, or EU/EEA students midway through a registered thesis with sizeable project costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm eligibility first: only Austrian, EEA citizens and equally treated stateless persons may apply under StudFG sections 3-4.
Look up your faculty's exact ECTS minimum and grade threshold in the current call before the window opens.
Have every exam registered in LFU:online with ECTS and grades, dated between 01 October and 30 September of the previous academic year.
Fill the LFU:online form completely, including bank name, IBAN and BIC, before forwarding it for processing.
For thesis scholarships, line up the supervisor expert opinion, full cost overview and financing plan weeks before the deadline.
Mark early May and late August in your calendar; these are the two months the university republishes its calls.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the hard closing date - the university states no applications can be accepted after it without exception.
Exceeding the maximum study duration (regular duration plus one semester); work or a second degree are not accepted as valid reasons.
Counting courses graded 'successfully completed' or using overall grade averages instead of individual grades.
Requesting thesis funding for living costs, tuition, binding, consumables or student-worker salaries, which are explicitly excluded.
Assuming an entitlement - applications always outnumber available slots and awards are purely ranked.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, health insurance and tuition fees are not covered by either scheme, and thesis costs such as binding, chemicals and staffing must be funded from other sources; recipients also stay liable for the Austrian student union fee.
document_audit: Only exams registered in LFU:online with ECTS and grades count; 'successfully completed' formative courses are ignored.
For recognitions, the actual examination date - not the recognition date - determines eligibility.
The overview of costs must be fully completed and signed by the expert, with away-from-home costs listed separately.
Literature purchases count only if the books are handed over to the university or faculty library after the thesis.
Recipients must keep invoices and receipts for a final report after completion.
alerts: Eligibility trap: non-EEA (third-country) nationals cannot apply, no matter how strong their record.
Timing trap: the AY 2025/26 windows closed on 02 October 2026; the 2026/27 call is expected in the same late-August to early-October slot.
The thesis scholarship has two shorter windows (early May and mid-September); the autumn one closes at the same time as the performance-based call.
Joint programmes with Innsbruck Medical University and UMIT can only be applied for at the University of Innsbruck.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through LFU:online during the published window; the College Service Center screens completeness, the faculty ranks and decides, and every applicant receives a written decision via LFU:online.
